long_biography.plain_text:
Benko left school after spending more time on building sites than in class, developing luxury apartments from Innsbruck attic space. In his early twenties he founded Immofina, later renamed Signa, and moved from redevelopment into trophy assets across European capitals. The group combined prime commercial property with department-store ownership, including Karstadt, KaDeWe and a stake in Selfridges.

Signa’s expansion relied on readily available debt and rising property values. When interest rates jumped and refinancing dried up, its holding company filed for insolvency in November 2023. Benko had already handed the advisory-board chair to a restructuring specialist; personal insolvency followed the next March. In July 2026, Austria’s Supreme Court upheld his conviction for insolvency-related fraud over a €300,000 transfer to his mother. Other proceedings remained unresolved.
